News Home Study at Lancaster Global Experiences Study abroad - Lancaster students Home Study at Lancaster Global Experiences Study abroad - Lancaster students Study Abroad Continue your university adventure in another country. Follow in the footsteps of hundreds of Lancaster students who have studied abroad as part of their degree for a year or term. As well as experiencing another culture, you will grow in confidence, independence and add new skills to your CV. Where can I go? You can use this list to find out the overseas partners where students from all Lancaster departments have studied abroad previously. These lists are only a guide on previous Study Abroad destinations are places available at overseas partners can vary each year. Where can I go? Costs There are costs associated with studying abroad. See the tabs below for more information. Tuition fees 2025-2026 Living costs Other costs Tab Content: Tuition fees 2025-2026 Tuition Fees You pay tuition fees to Lancaster University during your study period and you do not pay any tuition fees to your host university. If you study abroad for a full year, you pay 15%* of your normal tuition fee to Lancaster. For home students, this is approximately £1,431 for 2025/26. If you study abroad for one term, you will be charged your full tuition fee (100%). It is expected that tuition fees for 2026/27 will be announced in Spring 2026. For updated information please refer to our UK and EU fees webpage. Tab Content: Living costs Living Costs If you study abroad outside of the EU, you will be required to prove that you have funding to support yourself. Cost will vary by country. You do not have to have the full amount required in your bank account. You can show you have funds from different sources including your student loan, savings, scholarships, bursaries or from family. Country Cost in local currency Cost in Pounds (£) USA US $14,358 - $28,299 £11,743 – £23,240 Australia AUD $27,390 Approx. £15,598 Canada CND $10,164+ £6,000+ New Zealand NZD $20,000 Approx. £10,470 +flights Hong Kong HKD $120,000 Approx. £12,700 Tab Content: Other costs Other costs It is compulsory for you to have medical insurance when you are studying abroad. Depending on the country you are going to, this may mean taking out the host university's policy, a national student policy or finding your own. You are covered by Lancaster University's emergency travel policy when you are overseas. However, this is not a general health policy. You can see what is covered by the University's insurance policy, which can be found on the students' Study Abroad Moodle page, so you will also need appropriate travel insurance to cover your personal possessions while you are away. If you decide to study abroad, you will receive further information during the year before you go overseas. There may be funding available (e.g. Turing Scheme ) for you to apply to help fund your experience abroad. How do I apply? You apply through UCAS for degrees with Study Abroad in the title e.g. History (Study Abroad). If this is not available for your subject area, you apply when you start your degree. Some degree schemes do not allow a year or term abroad. The relevant department can confirm what is possible. There are limited options to study abroad for a term only. Below is a timeline for students studying abroad (excluding students studying in the School of Global Affairs). Study Abroad application process at Lancaster For most students, the Study Abroad application process once you are a Lancaster student will begin at the start of year 2. However, we want to make sure students are as prepared as possible for when the application process starts, so the Global Experiences team will deliver a number of information sessions throughout year 1, and you will also be invited to social events with Lancaster students who have previously completed the Study Abroad programme, as well as incoming exchange students from our partner universities and countries around the world where you may travel to for your placement. The table below gives an outline of what the Study Abroad application cycle at Lancaster will look like for you in the year before you study abroad. Please note that there are a small number of degree schemes where the options to study overseas is in year 2, and so this application cycle will take place in your 1st year at Lancaster. Please check your course pages for further information. Stage 1 Stage 2 Stage 3 Stage 4 Stage 5 Stage 1 October/November If you were admitted to the University on a Study Abroad degree scheme or if you are on a standard Lancaster degree scheme but want to study abroad, you should contact your Departmental Study Abroad Adviser to express an interest in participating. November/December The Global Experiences Office holds general information sessions for all students interested in studying abroad during November. There are also specific information and drop-in sessions starting in December about how much it costs to study abroad and immigration requirements. You then research exchange universities that are available for your department. You will be asked to provide your Departmental Study Abroad Advisor with a shortlist of your preferred universities by the end of the Michaelmas term. Stage 2 January/February Your Departmental Study Abroad Advisor will allocate you a place by mid-January. Stage 3 February/March The Global Experiences Office will send you information about how to apply to your host university. Applications are submitted by the end of Lent term. May/June You will receive your acceptance documents from your host university. Once you have received these documents, you must apply for your visa. Stage 4 June/July The Global Experiences Office will hold pre-departure briefings for students who are studying abroad. Attendance at one of these is compulsory. You will be told if you have fulfilled the academic requirements to study abroad following the Exam Boards in the Summer term. If you are studying in the USA, you will have to go to the US Embassy for an interview. Stage 5 July/August If you are studying in Australia or New Zealand, you will leave for your year abroad. August/September If you are studying in the USA, Canada, Europe or Asia, you will leave for your year abroad. Frequently asked questions accordion Show all sections Who can study abroad? Most Lancaster undergraduates have the opportunity to go abroad as part of their degree. However please check with your department as there are a few exceptions. Will the modules I take abroad count towards my Lancaster degree? Yes. The grades you achieve at your host university will be translated back and be credited to your Lancaster degree. Depending on your degree scheme and your academic department, the number of degree-related credits you will be required to study and translate back to your Lancaster Study Abroad degree will be different. What do I study when I am abroad? You will study a full credit load during the time you are overseas, and the number of degree-related modules you study will be determined by your academic department. Students on Integrated Master's will be required to study 100% of their credits in degree-related modules which match to your degree at Lancaster. For Bachelors students, there is more flexibility in the modules you take overseas and your departmental Study Abroad Advisor will support you in choosing modules for your Study Plan. You might also have the opportunity to take modules that are not available at Lancaster. When do I go? Most Study Abroad options are now part of a 4-year Bachelor's and Integrated Master's degree, meaning you will usually go abroad for a full year in your 3rd year before returning to Lancaster for year 4. Some departments/degrees have an alternative Study Abroad schedule (e.g. MEng Engineering, the Accounting and Finance department) so please consult the relevant course page for more information. Will I need a visa to study abroad? Depending on where you go, you will likely be required to get a student visa. You should check specific study visa requirements on the country's Embassy/consulate website. What support is there to help me through the process? There is a dedicated Global Experiences team who will guide you through the process. We hold scheduled information sessions, social events, one-to-one appointments and run drop in sessions during term time. If you have any questions, please email us at globalexperiences@lancaster.ac.uk . News Home Study at Lancaster International Students Global Summer Schools Home Study at Lancaster International Students Global Summer Schools Global Summer Schools Expand your global competencies, meet a network of students from across the world, and immerse yourself in a unique learning experience at a research-led university that’s consistently ranked in the top 15 in major UK league tables. Apply today Why choose Lancaster University Global Summer School? This fulfilling global experience will boost your academic and career prospects, while you gain a diverse network of students from around the world. You’ll be awarded an official transcript and earn Lancaster University academic credit upon successful completion of your summer school programme. What’s more, you’ll be taught by distinguished academics at a research-led university and learn at a beautiful parkland campus in the north-west of England. Please note: Global Summer Schools are not currently open to Lancaster, Bailrigg students. Applications close on Tuesday 07 April 2026. Apply today Sign up to our Mailing List Sign up to an Information Session Priceless lessons ''Three-week exchange taught me cross-cultural communication, independence, global perspectives, and lifelong friendships- priceless lessons beyond textbooks.''- North China University of Technology student, International Cultural Experience programme 2025. Our summer school programmes In 2025, we welcomed over 130 students from around the world onto our three-week summer schools. For 2026, we will be offering the following programmes: International Cultural Experience Gain an excellent understanding of British life and immerse yourself in the unique culture and explore contemporary topics. Programme dates: 06 - 24 July 2026. Film Develop an understanding of the formal and technical composition of films and the wider conventions of cinema. Programme dates: 06 - 24 July 2026 Leadership, Sustainability and Innovation Develop your leadership skills and sense of entrepreneurship as you work to fix real issues with local businesses and Non-Governmental Organisations. Programme dates: 06 - 24 July 2026. Social programme As well as the academic content, the Global Summer Schools offer a lively social programme with a wide range of opportunities to make friends, try new skills, and travel the UK with our organised group coach trips (a small fee will apply to cover the cost of travel). Our host of activities will help you make the most of your time here at Lancaster, and you’ll be accompanied by our friendly Student Ambassadors who will be there to help you throughout the three weeks. Plus, you’ll have free time to use as you wish. Social programme Lancaster's location The historic city of Lancaster, just 3 miles away from our campus, is located in the north-west of England. A welcoming campus, outstanding teaching, and a truly international student community. Lancaster University offers a high-quality study abroad experience at a leading UK university, combining excellent teaching with a supportive and welcoming campus environment. As a visiting study abroad or exchange student, you will study alongside Lancaster degree students and be taught by the same academic staff. You’ll choose from a range of undergraduate modules, while gaining first-hand experience of UK higher education. Lancaster is a campus-based university, with teaching spaces, accommodation, colleges, and student support services all in one place. This creates a strong sense of community and makes it easy for visiting students to settle in, access support, and get involved in university life. Beyond your studies, you can take part in student societies and sports, explore the historic city of Lancaster, and use the campus’s location to travel around the UK and beyond. With a diverse international student community and a strong focus on student support, Lancaster provides an inclusive and engaging environment for study abroad. Why Lancaster? Full Year: 120 LU credits / 30 US credits / 60 ECTS Michaelmas only: 40-60 LU credits / 10-15 US credits / 20-30 ECTS Lent/Summer only: 60-80 LU credits / 15-20 US credits / 30-40 ECTS Module Levels Undergraduate degrees in England take three years to complete, and modules are numbered to correspond with a Framework for Higher Education Qualifications (FHEQ) level: Level 4 - year one undergraduate Level 5 - year two undergraduate Level 6 - year three/final year undergraduate Level 7 - Postgraduate Taught (standalone master's or four year integrated master's) You must have completed a year of undergraduate study at your home university before coming to Lancaster. What can I study? Please find the modules available for study abroad students starting in September 2026 and January 2027 below. Study abroad modules Tab Content: Term dates You can study at Lancaster for: Michaelmas (September - December) Lent and Summer (January - June) Full academic year (September - June) You can also study for a calendar year (January - December) if that fits best at your home university. We also offer Lancaster Global Summer Schools in the early summer. NB: Postgraduate Erasmus+ students may have different terms. Please check the Erasmus+ postgraduate module handbook . Key dates for 2026/27 September starters: Students are expected to arrive on Saturday 26 September, or Sunday 27 September 2026 depending on their College allocation. Welcome Week: 28 September 2026 - 2 October 2026 Michaelmas Term: 5 October 2026 - 11 December 2026 If you are here for Michaelmas term only, you will likely have assignments to complete after the term has ended. Welcome Week: 4 January 2027 - 8 January 2027 Lent Term: 11 January 2027 - 19 March 2027 Summer term: 19 April 2027 – 25 June 2027 *Please note these term dates may be subject to change. For confirmation please consult the link below. Living Costs and Budgeting On-campus accommodation costs vary depending on the kind of room you choose; have a look at the 'quick cost comparison' table for a detailed breakdown. All students pay a small college membership fee, which supports the running of college events and activities. The fee for visiting study abroad students is £15. Insurance costs vary depending on the cover required. Rent on campus includes limited cover. Entertainment costs are excluded. Please budget for these according to your own needs You will also need to budget for: Visa Travel costs to and from Lancaster Health insurance if you are attending Lancaster for less than 6 months Textbooks Vacation and weekend travel Entertainment Telephone, laundry, cooking and eating utensils; and other personal expenses. These will obviously vary widely according to your budget, tastes and requirements. You can find budgeting advice and tips on how to get the most for your money whilst at Lancaster on our Managing your money ASK page. This is because we provide everything you need to live comfortably and safely: accommodation, facilities, social areas, green spaces, and so much more. Study and research takes place in a range of modern and state-of-the-art spaces. Take a virtual tour of our beautiful campus and discover what we can offer you. Lancaster provides multiple ways of joining in with sport , either on your own, as a member of your college or as a member of one of our many sport societies. Study abroad and global summer schools at Lancaster Vacation travel and summer schools Photograph: Student: Kelsey in Missouri, USA Travel during the vacation periods with fellow Lancaster students to destinations around the world, or take part in a summer school run by one of our global academic partners. Immerse yourself in the colourful nature of cultural exchange, explore a new country and gain perspective on global issues. Short-term travel opportunities Packaged programmes to our partners in Sunway University, Malaysia Partner summer schools Vacation travel partners Travel funding Photograph: Student: Joe in Inhambane, Mozambique We believe that cost should not be a barrier to global experiences. That’s why we offer a number of different grants to support students to travel, whether it’s for a field course to Europe, a summer school in Canada or a year in Australia. We are also proud to announce that Lancaster University has successfully been granted the Turing Scheme funding for 2024/2025. Additionally, there is also funding available for recent graduates taking part in overseas work, research, volunteering and internship opportunities. Discover funding opportunities Alex Hunter "Lancaster University has put the world at my fingertips. I travelled to the United States and China, yet Lancaster brings the world to campus as well via a diverse range of culturally immersive events and fun, engaging societies!" Alex Hunter 2016-2019, BA Politics & International Relations Gerta Ramaj "Going to a university where I have met and become close friends with people from all over the world, as well as giving me the opportunity to travel to Malaysia, has been an incredibly eye-opening and humbling experience." Gerta Ramaj 2015-2018, LLB Law Hayley Keohane "My study abroad year has made my experience at Lancaster a global one. Oregon State was an adventure, and my home away from home - made up of friends from across the world, diverse cultures, new ways of learning and a whole lot of fun" Hayley Keohane 2015-2018, MSci Geography Niamh Bush "My university experience has definitely been enhanced by engaging with people from different cultures in the global communities. It has given me the opportunity to broaden my horizons and make friends for life." Niamh Bush 2016-2019, BA Linguistics and English Language Molly McDonough “Being able to be part of a global community at Lancaster has enriched my time here. From living with people from a variety of different cultures in college life, to be being able to experience once in a lifetime trips, my Lancaster experience is truly global.” Molly McDonough 2015-2018, BA International Relations Global experiences on campus Coming to Lancaster is all about broadening your horizons, learning new subjects, finding new perspectives and discovering new experiences as part of a community that reaches around the world. You'll rub shoulders with students from over 100 countries, so you'll have every chance to make international connections of your own, on your course, in societies or socially. Learn a language International student societies Develop your global skills Undergraduate research conference Students in one of the chemistry labs. Each year Lancaster University hosts an online conference bringing together undergraduate students from around the Lancaster Partnership to showcase and celebrate research they have conducted – whether as part of a dissertation, internship, placement, or coursework. Undergraduate Research Conference Lancaster's global partners Lancaster is constantly developing partnerships worldwide to ensure it delivers teaching that takes students to the frontiers of knowledge and produces graduates who can compete in a global job market.
